chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Rehearsing with a Melody Maker-winning British band and touring England
summary: The poll-winning band is eager but young and underprepared in the postwar period, and they tour many English towns.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Anyway, after that, we had rehearsal with this band who had won the Melody Maker poll over there as being the band of the year. The Melody Maker is the English equivalent to Downbeat in the United States. I don't remember the name of this bandleader, but he was so happy to be working with Sarah Vaughan, the great Sarah Vaughan -- and all of the musicians as well.

When we went to rehearsal, we found out that the band wasn't really up to par as to the musicians we had been working with. Most of them were quite young, and this was in the Post-War period, where certain things were still being rationed in England at that particular time. We had quite a time with the rehearsal, and trying to get them to play the music as well as they could. But you know, they were very cooperative and doing the best they could, and of course, we were very patient with them, understanding that they weren't American musicians and didn't know as much as would be expected of them to play this music.

Nevertheless, we rehearsed a couple of days, and then we took off for this tour, which was a very extensive tour. I think we hit just about every hill and vale in England, little towns that I know of now that I wasn't very familiar with before. Towns like... Well, I knew about Newcastle, but...
